cluster_name: Trump halves US-South Korea drills while courting Kim Jong Un summit
event_summary: Trump ordered US-South Korea joint exercises halved and canceled the Ssangyong marine drill, both citing Iranian war force constraints. He posted old photos with Kim Jong Un signaling a summit; Pyongyang fired 10 short-range ballistic missiles in reply.
tldr: At the headline layer the story fractures along two axes: the security axis (drill cuts and cancellations dominate Defense News, NK News, The Hindu, and Korea Herald), and the diplomatic axis (Trump courting Kim for a summit dominates Daily Sabah, Deutsche Welle, KBS, and The Diplomat). The body-layer depth — North Korea's missile volley, Trump's 'denuclearization of Iran' verbal slip, and the deliberate omission of 'denuclearization' from official readouts — is almost entirely invisible at the RSS/homepage layer; only Yonhap surfaces the readout controversy in its title.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to frame Kim Jong Un as a simultaneous object of desire for three great powers — naming Trump, Putin, and Xi in a single title — a structural multipolar lens absent from all 18 other titles in the corpus.

The only outlet to surface the denuclearization-omission controversy at the headline level, naming 'omission from call readouts' as the explicit news hook rather than the cooperation-pledge formulation used by every other South Korean title.

The only headline in the corpus to adopt an interrogative 'Why Now?' register, treating Trump's outreach as a puzzle requiring explanation rather than a diplomatic event to be reported — the only analytical-frame title among 19.
The only headline linking Korean-theater force-availability shortfalls to concurrent US tanker withdrawals from Bulgaria, importing a European-theater angle that no other outlet's title carries.

bottom_line: The headline layer splits cleanly between drill-cut alarmism (Defense News, NK News, India, Korea Herald) and summit-diplomacy theater (Daily Sabah, DW, KBS, The Diplomat), suppressing the body-layer depth — North Korea's missile response, Trump's Iran-denuclearization verbal slip, and the deliberate omission of 'denuclearization' from official readouts — almost entirely from the RSS/homepage layer.
